WooCommerce → Shopify · Migration, two options

Gem Gardener — Shopify Migration Proposal

Client: Gem Gardener (gemgardener.com), fine jewellery, gems and objects
Prepared by: LitOS/LitGroup  ·  Date: November 5, 2026
$1,350Option 1 — 45hRebuild the current site on Shopify, with improvements (§3)
$1,950Option 2 — 65hFull redesign: 20h design + 45h build (§3)
EllaTheme, free through our partnership (§5)

You want to move gemgardener.com from WooCommerce to Shopify. This document gives you two ways to do it: rebuild the site as it is today with a few targeted improvements, or redesign it in a more editorial, luxury style. It also covers the appointment booking and the "Sell Your Jewellery" form, which need a different approach on Shopify.

1

AreaWhat we see todayWhat we'd do
HeaderMinimal header with a "Browse" button, even on desktop (§1.1)Show the main menu items directly on desktop; keep the drawer for mobile
MenuOne long drawer list: Shop, Jewelry, Gems, By Collection, account and contact all stacked (§1.2)Group into clear top-level paths, with product images inside the menu (§1.2)

1.1 Header

TodayThe header shows only the logo, a "Browse" button and search. It's clean, but on a desktop screen visitors have to open a drawer to see any category.

1.2 Menu

TodayEvery link sits in one long column. This works on a phone, but on desktop it hides your collections and mixes shopping links with "My Account" and "Appointment".

ReferenceAnother jewellery site, shown as an example only. We'd take the two-panel idea: categories on the left, image tiles for the open category on the right, and service links grouped at the bottom.

1.3 Homepage (Option 2)

ReferenceAnother jewellery site, shown as an example only. We'd take the full-width hero, centred logo and a single headline with one link, using your own photography.

1.4 Collection page (Option 2)

ReferenceAnother jewellery site, shown as an example only. We'd take the large tiles with lots of white space, a lifestyle image placed in the grid, and a simple "Filters" and "Sort by" bar.

2

Features that work differently on Shopify

2.1 Appointment booking

Shopify has no built-in booking. We set up a booking app from the Shopify App Store, connect it to the "Appointment" link and style it to match the site. We'll suggest one once you confirm what a booking needs (§4).

2.2 "Sell Your Jewellery" form

Your current Sell Your Jewellery page lets visitors send details of a piece. Shopify's built-in contact form can't take file uploads, so customers couldn't attach photos with it.

Two ways to handle this:

  • Form app: a form builder app adds a photo upload field.
  • No app: keep the native form for the text details and ask customers to reply with photos by email.

7

Who configures what

Payment and shipping are set up by you in your Shopify admin. We guide you and verify the result, but we don't enter the credentials. They give access to your money and your carrier rates, so they stay with the account holder.

ItemYou doWe do
Payment providerOpen the account, enter the credentials, run the first live orderRecommend a provider, give you a step-by-step guide, test checkout
Shipping zones & ratesEnter zones and rates, keep them up to dateCopy your current WooCommerce rules into a rate sheet, walk you through it, test real addresses
Apps (§2)Install and pay for the apps you chooseConfigure and style them, test bookings and form submissions
